findings.description: The Lambda function's environment variables contain a literal AWS access key ID and secret access key ("AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE" / "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY"). These credentials are stored in Terraform state and in the Lambda's environment in plaintext, are readable by anyone with GetFunction access, and cannot be rotated without a redeploy. Secrets should be sourced from Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store at runtime, with the execution role granted least-privilege access to fetch them.

The function is configured with runtime "nodejs12.x", which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS. Running an unsupported runtime leaves known vulnerabilities in the Node.js runtime and its bundled dependencies unpatched in the execution environment.

findings.issue_category: Missing KMS encryption of environment variables
findings.description: The environment block holding the embedded credentials is not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key via kms_key_arn; the values are protected only by the AWS-owned default key. Combining this with the plaintext secrets in the same block means the secrets are not covered by any key whose access policy the tenant controls. (Note: this is reported only as it relates to the secret exposure; absent customer-managed keys alone would ordinarily be a hardening observation.)
